1. We have reviewed the accompanying Statement of standalone unaudited financial results of Delta Corp

year to-date results for the period from April 01, 2026 to September 30, 2026 ('the Statement') attached

2.

This Statement, which is the responsibility of Company's Management and has been approved by the
Company's Board of Directors, has been prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement
principles laid down in Indian Accounting Standard 34 'Interim Financial Reporting', prescribed under
Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 ('the Act'), read with relevant rules issued thereunder ('Ind AS
34' ), and other recognized accounting principles generally accepted in India, and is in compliance with
the Regulations. Our responsibility is to express a conclusion on the Statement based on our review.

3. We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagement (SRE)
2410, "Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity"
issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. A review of interim financial information
consists of making inquiries, primarily of persons responsible for financial and accounting matters, and
applying analytical and other review procedures. A review is substantially less in scope than an audit

consequently does not enable us to obtain assurance that we would become aware of all significant

4.

measurement principles laid down in Ind AS 34 and other recognised accounting principles generally

including the manner in which it is to be disclosed, or that it contains any material misstatement.

 Notes to the standalone financial results:
1. The above results for the quarter and half year ended 30 th September, 2026 which have been subjected to review
by Statutory Auditors of the Company were reviewed and recommended by the Audit Committee and
subsequently approved by the Board of Directors at its meeting held on 19th October, 2026, in terms of Regulation
33 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.
2.

On 27th September, 2023 the Company and its two subsidiary companies namely Highstreet Cruises &
Entertainment Private Limited and Delta Pleasure Cruise Company Private Limited received show cause notices
from the Directorate General of GST Intelligence, Hyderabad, for alleged short payment of Goods and Service
Tax (GST) aggregating~ 16,822.98 Crores under Section 74(1) of the CGST Act, 2017 and Goa SGST Act, 2017 for
the period from 1st July, 2017 to 31 st March, 2022 and Deltatech Gaming Limited ("DGL") 'the erstwhile associate
Company', received show cause notice dated 28th October, 2023 for alleged short payment of Goods and Service
Tax (GST) aggregating ~ 6,384.32 Crores for the period pt July, 2017 to 30 th November, 2022 from Director
General of GST Intelligence, Kolkata.
Additionally on 17th March, 2026, the Company along with its one subsidiary, Highstreet Cruises & Entertainment
Private Limited and on 25 th September 2026, Delta Pleasure Cruise Company Private Limited received show cause
notice from Office of The Commissioner of Commercial Taxes, Goa for alleged short payment of GST aggregating
~ 1,883.96 Crores under Section 74(1) of the CGST Act, 2017 and Goa SGST Act, 2017 for the period from pt April,
2022 to 3pt March, 2023.
The Company/ subsidiary companies/ erstwhile associate company, as mentioned above, had filed Writ petitions
and had obtained stay order from respective High Courts on show cause notices for the period from pt July, 2017
to 30 th November, 2022. The Union of India had sought the transfer of all similar Writ Petitions of the entire
Industry pending at various High Courts to the Hon'ble Supreme Court and same had been admitted by the
Hon'ble Supreme Court.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court pronounced its judgment dated 27 th May, 2026 in matters relating to GST
applicability on on line gaming, betting, gambling and casino transactions. Pursuant to the said judgment, pending
proceedings are required to be adjudicated in accordance with the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme
Court and the applicable valuation provisions under the CGST Rules.
Subsequently, the Company received adjudication orders in relation to the aforesaid proceedings for the period
1st July, 2017 to 31 st March, 2022 wherein the GST demand for casino transactions was determined under Rule
31C of the CGST rules of~ 78.56 Crores. Further, the Company also received adjudication orders for mixed supply
for the aforesaid period of~ 93.80 Crores.
Based on the aforesaid orders and the principles laid by the Supreme Court's judgement, the Company has
computed the GST provision for the period July, 2017 to September, 2023 in respect of casino transactions and
for the period July, 2017 to September, 2025 in respect of mixed supply and recognised total provision (including
interest) aggregating to~ 319.60 Crores in the standalone results as at 30 th September, 2026 as Exceptional Item
(including~ 200.62 Crores provision recognised during the quarter ended 30th June, 2026).
The Company has made provision on prudence basis and reserves all rights to contest and litigate the aforesaid
matter before the appropriate authorities/ forums. Based on legal advice and management's assessment, the
Company believes that it has strong grounds to contest the entire demand for mixed supply and interest levied
on the GST demand determined under Rule 31C. Subsequent to the balance sheet date, the Company has paid
the principal amount of liability to the tune of ~ 49 Crores under Rule 31C as per adjudication order for the
period 1st July, 2017 to 31 st March, 2022.

 Supreme Court dated 27th May, 2026, management has reassessed and concluded that the Company will no
longer be required to indemnify the buyer towards GST liability in respect of alleged short payment of GST.
The Company has investments in equity shares in the aforesaid two subsidiaries aggregating~ 650.58 Crores and
has provided short-term loans aggregating~ 249.72 Crores as at 30th September, 2026. Based on management's
assessment of the recoverable amounts from such subsidiaries, no provision for impairment is currently required.
Also, the Company has investment amounting~ 159.08 Crores in erstwhile associate Company which have been
fully provided for in previous year being investment in an on line gaming company.
3. The Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held on 6th December, 2024, approved the Revised
Composite Scheme of Arrangement amongst Delta Corp Limited, Deltin Hotel & Resorts Private Limited, Delta
Penland Limited and Deltin Cruises and Entertainment Private Limited and their respective shareholders and
creditors, for which approvals from NSE and BSE have been obtained. Pursuant to the order dated 18th June,
2026, passed by the Mumbai Bench of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), meetings of the shareholders
and sundry creditors were convened on 13th August, 2026, wherein the Scheme was duly approved by the
shareholders and creditors of the Company. The Scheme is proposed to be effective from 1st April, 2025 and
pending receipt of the remaining requisite statutory and regulatory approvals, no adjustments have been made
in the standalone financial results.
4.

During the last quarter, Company has closed down its operation in "Deltin Denzong Casino, Sikkim" to improve
operational efficiency and long-term profitability.

5.

Writ Petition No. 317 of 2019, filed before the Hon'ble Bombay High Court inter alia seeking directions to grant
a license under Section 13A of the Goa, Daman and Diu Public Gambling Act, 1976 for installation of electronic
amusement/slot machines at The Deltin Hotel, Daman has been dismissed by the Hon'ble Court vide its order
dated 29 th April, 2026. The Holding Company has filed Special leave petition in Supreme Court against High Court
order, which has been admitted.

6.

Due to flooding caused by heavy monsoon rains on 23 rd July, 2026, operations at The Deltin, Daman were
suspended for 37 days during the quarter ended 30 th September, 2026, adversely impacting hospitality revenue
for the quarter. The Hotel has resumed its normal operations from 29th August, 2026.

On 27th September, 2023 the Holding Company and its two subsidiary companies namely Highstreet Cruises &
Entertainment Private Limited and Delta Pleasure Cruise Company Private Limited ("the Group"} received show
cause notices from the Directorate General of GST Intelligence, Hyderabad, for alleged short payment of Goods
and Service Tax (GST} aggregating, 16,822.98 Crores under Section 74(1} of the CGST Act, 2017 and Goa SGST
Act, 2017 for the period from 1st July, 2017 to 31 st March, 2022 and Deltatech Gaming Limited ("DGL"} 'the
erstwhile associate Company', received show cause notice dated 28th October, 2023 for alleged short payment
of Goods and Service Tax (GST} aggregating, 6,384.32 Crores for the period pt July, 2017 to 30 th November,
2022 from Director General of GST Intelligence, Kolkata.
Additionally on 17th March, 2026 and on 25 th September, 2026, the Group received show cause notices from
Office of The Commissioner of Commercial Taxes, Goa for alleged short payment of GST aggregating, 1,883.96
Crores under Section 74(1) of the CGST Act, 2017 and Goa SGST Act, 2017 for the period from pt April, 2022 to
31st March, 2023.
The Holding Company/ subsidiary companies/ erstwhile associate company, as mentioned above, had filed Writ
petitions and had obtained stay order from respective High Courts on show cause notices for the period from pt
July, 2017 to 30th November, 2022. The Union of India had sought the transfer of all similar Writ Petitions of the
entire Industry pending at various High Courts to the Hon'ble Supreme Court and same had been admitted by
the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court pronounced its judgment dated 27 th May, 2026 in matters relating to GST
applicability on on line gaming, betting, gambling and casino transactions. Pursuant to the said judgment, pending
proceedings are required to be adjudicated in accordance with the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme
Court and the applicable valuation provisions under the CGST Rules.
Subsequently, the Group received adjudication orders in relation to the aforesaid proceedings for the period 1st
July, 2017 to 3pt March, 2022 wherein the GST demand for casino transactions was determined under Rule 31C
of the CGST rules of, 151.15 Crores. Further, the Group also received adjudication orders for mixed supply for
the aforesaid period of, 125.27 Crores.

 Based on the aforesaid orders and the principles laid by the Hon'ble Supreme Court's judgement, the Group has
computed the GST provision for the period July, 2017 to September, 2023 in respect of casino transactions and
for the period July, 2017 to September, 2025 in respect of mixed supply and recognised total provision (including
interest) aggregating to ~ 443.65 Crores in the consolidated results as at 30 th September, 2026 as Exceptional
Item (including~ 306.73 Crores provision recognised during the quarter ended 30 th June, 2026).
The Group has made provision on prudence basis and reserves all rights to contest and litigate the aforesaid
matter before the appropriate authorities/ forums. Based on legal advice and management's assessment, the
Group believes that it has strong grounds to contest the entire demand for mixed supply and interest levied on
the GST demand determined under Rule 31C. Subsequent to the balance sheet date, the Group has paid the
principal amount of liability to the tune of~ 80.97 Crores under Rule 31C as per adjudication order for the period
1st July, 2017 to 31st March, 2022.
Further, pursuant to the Share Purchase and Investment Agreement dated 20th February, 2025 read with
amended agreement dated 19th March, 2025, entered into between Delta Corp Limited, DGL and Head Digital
Works Private Limited (buyer) in relation to sale of stake of DGL, and considering the judgment of the Hon'ble
Supreme Court dated 27 th May, 2026, management has reassessed and concluded that the Group will no longer
be required to indemnify the buyer towards GST liability in respect of alleged short payment of GST.
The Holding Company carries Goodwill amounting to ~ 93.51 Crores pertaining to above mentioned two
subsidiary companies. Based on the assessment of the recoverable amounts, management has determined that
no impairment towards Goodwill and other assets relating to the two subsidiaries is currently required. The
Holding company also carries investment in erstwhile associate amounting to ~ 240.26 Crores which had been
fully provided for in previous year being investment in online gaming company.
6. The Board of Directors of the Holding Company, at its meeting held on 6th December, 2024, approved the Revised
Composite Scheme of Arrangement amongst Delta Corp Limited, Deltin Hotel & Resorts Private Limited, Delta
Penland Limited and Deltin Cruises and Entertainment Private Limited and their respective shareholders and
creditors, for which approvals from NSE and BSE have been obtained. Pursuant to the order dated 18th June,
